narrative.overview: Britannia Crown reads like a trusted family advisor's study, not a marketplace stall: a deep burgundy and champagne palette borrowed from British heritage branding, paired with a serif display face for authority and a light, airy sans body face for warmth. The system exists to make a family relocating to Dubai feel they are handing their child's education to a confident, established partner — never a discount tutoring aggregator, never a cold corporate portal. The system explicitly rejects generic template energy: no stock-agency blue-and-white SaaS look, no discount-marketplace badges or urgency banners, no gimmicky animation. Confidence is conveyed through restraint — generous whitespace, one accent color used sparingly, and real numbers instead of decorative flourish.
keyCharacteristics: Deep burgundy + champagne as the only real color statement; everything else is neutral
Serif display type (Cormorant Garamond) for every heading, paired with a light-weight sans (Jost) for body copy
Flat-by-default surfaces; shadow appears only as a hover response, never at rest
Pill-shaped tags/badges contrasted against sharp 2-4px corners everywhere else
Wide, generous section padding (100px desktop) — nothing feels cramped or ad-dense

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Champagne is the only color used to signal "act here." It never appears twice in the same viewport for two different purposes.

rules.name: The Uppercase Whisper Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase, wide-tracked labels (eyebrows, nav, stat labels) never exceed 13px. They organize the page without competing with headline serif type for attention.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest. If it's not being hovered or focused, it sits flush against its background.

dos: Do keep champagne (#E8C89C) as the only "act here" signal — one accent, used sparingly (the One Accent Rule).
Do use uppercase, wide-tracked labels (≤13px) for all structural/meta text — eyebrows, nav, stat labels, button labels.
Do keep cards and buttons flat at rest; only add shadow/lift on hover or focus.
Do pair every headline in Cormorant Garamond with body copy in Jost — never mix another display or body face into a page.
Do favor real, specific numbers over decorative claims when building trust-building sections.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color alongside champagne — it dilutes the One Accent Rule.
Don't use rounded/pill shapes on buttons or cards — pill shape is reserved exclusively for tags/badges.
Don't add resting shadows to cards, buttons, or inputs — this system is flat-until-touched.

Don't let this drift toward a generic SaaS/template look (blue gradients, glassmorphism, urgency badges, countdown timers) — that directly contradicts the boutique-consultancy positioning in PRODUCT.md.
Don't use bold weight for emphasis in body copy — emphasis is carried by champagne color and italic serif, not font-weight jumps.
